entries.gloss: yes/no question marker, placed before the verb
entries.source: Alexander & Elias-Bursać, Bosnian, Croatian, Serbian, a Textbook (2nd ed., 2010), Lesson One grammar note, p. 3: "The most frequent way in S is to place da li before the verb, and the most frequent way in B and C is to place li after the verb."
entries.notes: A syntactic (word-order) variant rather than a lexical substitution, but explicitly source-attested and directly relevant to how a B/C/S mechanics analysis pass should treat question formation. Both "da li X" and "X li" produce the identical yes/no question; the difference is standard-preference, not meaning.

entries.gloss: yes/no question marker, placed after the verb
entries.source: Alexander & Elias-Bursać, Bosnian, Croatian, Serbian, a Textbook (2nd ed., 2010), Lesson One grammar note, p. 3
entries.notes: See "da li" entry - same question-formation function, opposite standard preference. "li" also appears as a clitic in Serbian in less formal/frequent placements per the same source note, so this B/C boundary is the dominant pattern rather than an absolute rule - flagged for the eventual mechanics-analysis pass rather than treated as a hard boundary here.
